The Customs chief disclosed that the Service generated N7.28 trillion in 2025, exceeding its target of N6.58 trillion, while collections reached approximately N4.03 trillion in the first half of 2026 against an annual target of N11.07 trillion. He said the figures demonstrated the growing importance of Customs to Nigeria’s public finances and the need to close revenue leakages without placing unnecessary burdens on legitimate businesses. Adeniyi said Customs revenue was not merely a federal government resource, explaining that import duties contributed to the Federation Account and were distributed among the three tiers of government. Under the allocation formula he cited, the Federal Government receives 52.68 per cent, states 26.72 per cent and local governments 20.60 per cent. He added that, under the new tax laws, 90 per cent of value-added tax collected on imports was allocated to states and local governments. “When a smuggler evades duty, he does not cheat an abstraction called government. He cheats a pupil, a nurse and a farmer,” he said. Adeniyi traced the Service’s revenue growth from N3.2 trillion in 2023 to N6.105 trillion in 2024 and N7.28 trillion in 2025, attributing the improvement to stronger compliance, improved valuation, digital systems and enforcement. He said the Service was determined to meet its 2026 target by reducing revenue leakages rather than obstructing legitimate trade. “We will pursue the target through compliance, data and facilitation, not through harassment at the ports, because a target met by choking trade would be a false victory,” he said. The Customs chief also cited the need to address illicit financial flows and trade misinvoicing, through which importers and exporters manipulate the declared value or description of goods to evade taxes, duties and other financial obligations. He said such practices weakened the country’s revenue base and undermined the integrity of its trade system. Adeniyi noted that Africa’s tax-to-GDP ratio stood at about 16.1 per cent, compared with approximately 33.9 per cent for countries in the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, highlighting the continent’s broader challenge of mobilising domestic revenue. He said Customs had a critical role to play in closing the gap by improving the accuracy of declarations, strengthening risk assessment and ensuring that eligible transactions were properly assessed. Adeniyi said the Service was deploying digital platforms and data analytics to improve the assessment of imports, detect suspicious declarations and reduce delays at the ports. He disclosed that the B’Odogwu cargo-processing platform handled approximately 16,000 entries and generated N120 billion in revenue in its first three months at the Port and Terminal Multi-Services Limited Command. He said the National Single Window, which went live on March 27, 2026, was intended to connect trade-related government processes and reduce duplication in documentation. “A study conducted at Tin Can Island Port showed that cargo release took almost five days on average, with more than 90 per cent of the time spent waiting.“ The Service, he said, was working towards reducing cargo clearance to 24 hours in the long term, with an interim target of two days and a plan to rely on scanning rather than physical examination for 99 per cent of cargo. He added that 51 companies certified under the Authorised Economic Operator programme had reduced their clearance time from 168 hours to 41 hours, while demurrage costs fell by approximately 90 per cent. According to him, the improvements showed that revenue collection and trade facilitation could reinforce each other when procedures were efficient and compliance was properly managed. Adeniyi said revenue protection could not be separated from national security, citing the interception of 399 pump-action rifles and hundreds of firearm components concealed in a container discharged from the vessel MV Velika at Tin Can Island Port in July 2026. The weapons were handed over to the National Centre for the Control of Small Arms and Light Weapons, while the case remained before the Federal High Court. He also recalled the seizure of 844 rifles and 112,500 rounds of ammunition at Onne, Rivers State, in June 2024, as well as the handover of 1,599 firearms seized between 2018 and 2024 to the national centre in February 2025. The Customs chief said the Service had also intercepted 25 containers of fake and unregistered medicines worth approximately N9.2 billion in July 2025. On wildlife trafficking, he cited the seizure of 3.76 tonnes of pangolin scales in Lagos in April 2025, representing at least 1,900 animals, and said enforcement operations since 2021 had led to seizures of more than 25 tonnes of pangolin scales and over one tonne of ivory, with 12 convictions secured. He also highlighted fuel smuggling, drug trafficking and the illegal movement of food commodities as activities that threatened public safety, economic stability and government revenue. On border management, Adeniyi argued that intelligence-led enforcement and cooperation with neighbouring countries were more sustainable than blanket border closures. He said Nigeria’s land-border closure between August 2019 and December 2020 curtailed some smuggling activities but did not eliminate the networks behind the illegal trade. “The lesson is that a nation is protected by intelligent control of its border, not by sealing it. Closure is a blunt instrument, while intelligence, data and joint patrols with our neighbours are sharper ones,” he said. He called for closer cooperation with border communities and neighbouring countries, while urging traders to use legitimate channels under regional trade arrangements such as the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme. Adeniyi also said Nigeria’s participation in the African Continental Free Trade Area depended on effective customs administration to verify the origin of goods and ensure that preferential trade arrangements were properly implemented. Imports from other African countries accounted for approximately four per cent of Nigeria’s total imports in 2025, he said, suggesting significant room for expanding intra-African trade. The Comptroller-General proposed a structured partnership with the University of Ibadan’s Centre of Excellence in Security Management to improve research on border economies, trade compliance and illicit financial flows. His proposals included a Border Economies Research Partnership focusing on locations such as Idiroko, Seme, Jibia and Illela; Customs Data and Analytics Fellowships; and an Illicit Trade Observatory to track trafficking in firearms, drugs, counterfeit medicines, wildlife products and fuel. He also called for independent academic evaluations of the Customs Act 2023, import duty waivers, the Authorised Economic Operator programme and the National Single Window

item.title: Meet Nigeria’s youngest female SAN, Olamide Ehinfun-Adekunle
item.description: Olamide Mojigbotoluwa Ehinfun-Adekunle has made history as Nigeria’s youngest female Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), attaining the prestigious legal rank at the age of 40. She was among 68 legal practitioners sworn in as Senior Advocates of Nigeria by the Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, on October 12, 2026, during the opening of the 2026/2027 legal year. Four women were among the newly elevated practitioners. Born on June 25, 1986, in Kaduna State, Ehinfun-Adekunle hails from Ijero-Ekiti in Ekiti State. Her journey into the legal profession began with her studies at Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife, where she obtained her Bachelor of Laws degree between 2003 and 2009. She proceeded to the Nigerian Law School, where she studied from 2009 to 2010, before earning a Master of Laws degree in International Trade Law from the University of Leeds, United Kingdom, between 2011 and 2012. She is also a member of the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators in the UK. Before joining Afe Babalola & Co. in September 2013, Ehinfun-Adekunle worked at D. D. Dodo & Co. and the Nuhu Ribadu Campaign Organisation. She subsequently became a partner at Afe Babalola & Co., where her areas of practice include complex litigation, commercial dispute resolution, oil and gas, arbitration, election petitions, transactional law and regulatory compliance. Her professional experience has also included appearances before the Court of Appeal and the Supreme Court of Nigeria. The Legal Practitioners’ Privileges Committee approved her elevation to the rank of SAN on July 23, 2026, before she was formally sworn in alongside 67 other legal practitioners in October. Ehinfun-Adekunle’s interest in law reportedly developed during her childhood. Her parents described her as talkative, a trait also reflected in her primary school reports. Stories told by her father about politics in the old Western Region and the legal career of Chief Rotimi Williams, popularly known as “Timi the Law”, helped shape her interest in the profession. Several prominent figures have influenced her career, including Aare Afe Babalola, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, Kehinde Ogunwumiju and Pastor R. A. Ogunwole. Beyond her legal practice, Ehinfun-Adekunle has spoken about the challenges confronting Nigeria’s justice system, particularly delays in the administration of justice and the financial burden prolonged litigation places on individuals and businesses. item.title: Imo Kidnap: Five Suspects Plead Not Guilty To Abducting Corps Members, Four Others
item.description: Five suspects accused of kidnapping 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members and four other persons in Imo State have pleaded not guilty to the charges against them following their arraignment before the Justice Oputa State High Court in Owerri. The defendants face a three-count charge bordering on conspiracy, hostage-taking and unlawful possession of firearms. Three of the suspects — 25-year-old Usman Aliyu, also known as Chonge; 21-year-old Babangida Aliyu; and 23-year-old Mohammed Ali, alias Smallie Pepper — are accused of abducting the prospective corps members on October 1, 2026, Nigeria’s Independence Day. According to the charge sheet, the trio allegedly demanded and collected ₦48 million and an undisclosed amount in US dollars for the release of the victims. They were also accused of unlawfully possessing three AK-47 rifles, four magazines, a pistol and 81 rounds of live ammunition. The prosecuting counsel said the charge of conspiracy to commit hostage-taking is punishable under Section 6 of the Imo State Prohibition of Hostage Taking and Related Offences Law No. 4 of 2009. The other two defendants, 27-year-old Aminu Haliru and 20-year-old Tange Ibrahim, also known as Jijji, are accused of abducting four persons around Owerri and Mgbidi on October 4, four days after the first abduction. The prosecution alleged that Haliru, Ibrahim and other suspects still at large collected ₦8 million for the release of the four victims. They also face allegations of unlawfully possessing an AK-47 rifle and a pump-action gun. The presiding judge, Justice Emeka Orafu, adjourned the trial until Thursday, October 22, 2026. The victims were abducted by gunmen near Umunoha in Mbaitoli Local Government Area on October 1, 2026, while travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, to their assigned NYSC orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. The abduction sparked a security operation to locate the victims and apprehend those responsible. On October 7, the 20 prospective corps members and the civilian were rescued from the Amakohia-Ubi forest in Owerri West Local Government Area. They subsequently received medical attention at the DSS hospital in Owerri. The DSS later arrested five suspects in intelligence-led operations conducted between October 10 and 14 in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, and Aba, Abia State. The operations involved a joint security team led by the DSS, working with the military, police and other security operatives. Three other suspects reportedly escaped with gunshot wounds, prompting a manhunt for them and other fleeing members of the suspected kidnapping syndicate. The arraignment marks a further step in the investigation into the abduction, as the prosecution of the five arrested suspects gets underway. item.title: Eniola Badmus apologises to Laide Bakare, calls for end to feud
item.description: Nollywood actress Eniola Badmus has apologised to her colleague, Laide Bakare, following the backlash over her reaction to Bakare’s name during a recent podcast appearance, expressing a desire to put their differences behind them. Badmus tendered the apology in a statement shared on Instagram on Tuesday, days after a clip from her appearance on Isbae U’s Curiosity Made Me Ask podcast went viral on social media. During the interview, the host mentioned Bakare as one of his favourite actresses, prompting Badmus to hiss and change her facial expression. The moment attracted reactions online and revived discussions about the strained relationship between the two actresses. Reflecting on her reaction via her Instagram page, Badmus admitted that it could have been perceived as dismissive and expressed regret over how it came across. “On reflection, I realise my reaction when Laide Bakare’s name was mentioned during my recent interview could have come across as dismissive, and for that, I sincerely apologise,” she wrote. Addressing Bakare directly, the actress added, “Laide, whatever our differences, I choose peace and I genuinely wish you well.” Badmus said maturity involves learning from past experiences and choosing to move forward rather than holding on to disagreements. “We’re all growing, learning and becoming better versions of ourselves. Sometimes maturity is simply knowing when to let go and move forward,” she stated. She concluded her message with a plea for peace, writing, “Joo maa binu. No negativity. No grudges. Let love lead and peace reigns.” The apology comes amid a history of public disagreements between the actresses, whose relationship has been marked by exchanges on social media and confrontations at public events. In March 2024, Badmus appeared to mock Bakare’s outfit at the latter’s book launch. Bakare had attended the event in a white outfit with an orange cape, which generated mixed reactions online. Badmus subsequently took to Instagram and wrote, “Ewo ninu yin lo wo Aso Pastor Ajidara. Abeg who??” The remark was widely interpreted as a dig at Bakare’s outfit. Bakare expressed disappointment over the incident, questioning why a colleague she regarded as a childhood friend from their University of Ibadan days would publicly criticise her instead of celebrating her achievement. item.title: #EndSARS: No Nigerian should be punished for demanding good governance – Obi
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has said no Nigerian should be punished for demanding good governance, as he marked six years since the October 20, 2020, incident at the Lekki Toll Gate. “Nigeria must become a nation where no citizen is punished for demanding good governance and a better future,” Obi said in a statement posted on X on Tuesday. Obi described the anniversary as a reminder of the price Nigerian youths paid in their demand for a better country. “Today, October 20, 2026, marks the sixth anniversary of the Lekki Toll Gate shootings, a painful reminder of the price Nigerian youths paid in their demand for a better country.” He recalled the events of October 20, 2020, saying peaceful protesters faced gunfire and that lives were lost, and many people were injured, leaving questions about justice, accountability and the value placed on human life. “On that fateful night, peaceful #EndSARS protesters were met with gunfire. Lives were lost, many were injured, and the nation was left with questions about justice, accountability, and the sanctity of human life.” Calling on Nigerians to remember the victims and resist treating injustice as normal, Obi said: “We must never forget. We must never normalise injustice.” He also noted that the anniversary reinforced his belief in a “New Nigeria,” describing it as a country where citizens are protected, young people are heard, and those in government exercise power responsibly and respect human rights. “As we remember the victims, I reaffirm my belief that a New Nigeria is possible—a country where citizens are protected, not brutalised; where young people are heard, not silenced; and where government power is exercised with responsibility and respect for human rights.” Obi added that the victims’ sacrifice should strengthen efforts to ensure the incident is not repeated while praying for those who died. “May the souls of the departed continue to rest in peace. May their sacrifice strengthen our resolve to build a Nigeria where this tragedy will never be repeated.” He ended the statement by reiterating his vision of a country where every life matters. The Lagos State Judicial Panel of Inquiry’s 2021 report found that Nigerian Army officers shot, injured and killed unarmed protesters at the Lekki Toll Gate, and said the manner of assault and killing could be described as a massacre in context. Vanguard reported that the panel identified at least 48 protesters who were shot, injured or assaulted. item.title: Uduaghan’s demise, shocking, great loss to Nigeria – Akpabio
item.description: Says his tenure as the state Governor marked a very significant moment in the infrastructural development of the state By Henry Umoru ABUJA- THE President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio has mourned the death of former Governor of Delta State, Dr. Emmanuel Uduaghan who died just three days before his 72nd birthday, according to his family. Akpabio has said Uduaghan’s tenure as the state Governor marked a very significant moment in the infrastructural development of the state as he described his death as shocking, a great loss to Nigeria and the entire people of the Niger Delta region. In a statement signed yesterday by his Special Assistant on Media, Jackson Udom, Akpabio said, “I received with profound shock and disbelief the news of the transition of Dr Uduaghan at the age of 71, just three days to his 72nd birthday. “Dr Uduaghan was the governor of Delta State from 2007- 2015, when I also had the opportunity to preside over the affairs of Akwa Ibom State as their governor. He was a distinguished medical doctor and a committed statesman, who devoted his life to public office. ” His tenure as the state Governor marked a very significant moment in the infrastructural development of the state. He was a committed leader to the healthcare delivery and human capital development of his people. He was a bridge-builder across the Niger Delta region and Nigeria as a whole. item.title: Power outage hits Google Cloud services, disrupting UK banks
item.description: A power outage at a Google Cloud data centre near London caused serious failures to services on Tuesday, the US technology giant said, as several UK banks reported widespread disruptions. Google said in a service update that its Cloud services suffered an outage “due to a power event”, adding that a full recovery was expected at around 1300 GMT on Tuesday. Services for the digital bank Revolut, including withdrawals from ATMs, bank transfers and bank card top-ups, were disrupted, which a source close to the matter attributed to the Google Cloud failures. UK lenders Lloyds and HSBC also confirmed customers were facing issues with their banking services. Google said the incident began at 0608 GMT on Tuesday. “Multiple Google Cloud services are experiencing elevated errors and intermittent network failures in europe-west2 region,” Google said in an earlier update, referring to its London data centre. Internet service tracker Downdetector indicated that hundreds of reports had been made of problems affecting other businesses, including the property website Rightmove and the Royal Mail postal service. Lloyds said it was aware “some customers are having issues with our app and online banking”. HSBC confirmed that customers were experiencing “difficulties accessing our services” and said that it would “monitor the situation, which is also affecting other organisations”. A Revolut spokesperson said the bank was “working to fix the issue since it was identified” and offered its apologies “to anyone affected and for any inconvenience caused”. “We can confirm that all our customers’ money and data are safe,” the spokesperson added in a statement. item.title: Mourinho warns no ‘untouchable’ stars at Real Madrid
item.description: Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho on Tuesday warned Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior and the team’s other stars that no-one is “untouchable”. Vinicius has struggled for form this season and is serving a four-match ban in La Liga for hair-pulling, but is available as Madrid host RB Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday. Ivorian winger Yan Diomande, the club’s record 140 million euro ($157m) signing, has impressed in recent weeks, scoring against Sevilla on Sunday in La Liga in Vinicius’s absence. “Only the club badge is untouchable,” Mourinho told reporters when asked if Vinicius’s place in the team was in danger given Diomande’s form. “I don’t like the concept of untouchable players. “What makes a player untouchable is not his status, the armband, his years at the club, how much was paid for him, what makes him untouchable is his performance on the pitch.” Mourinho said Vinicius would play on the left wing against Leipzig and he had not yet told Diomande whether he would start as well. Madrid host the Bundesliga side aiming for a third Champions League victory from three matches in the league phase, but in La Liga they are third and six points behind leaders Barcelona, who they visit on Sunday. Mourinho said the team’s level is still a long way from where he hopes he can take it. “A long way off… we’ve been here three or four months, it’s impossible to be where we want to be,” continued the veteran Portuguese coach. “We always have to improve, be it individually or collectively… I understand the demands (at this club) are the maximum. “I’ve been here three years (2010-2013), and so I know perfectly well how things are. I can’t lose my direction… (even though) I know there is a lot of work to do.” French defender Ibrahima Konate said the former Chelsea and Manchester United coach commanded respect. “He’s a great manager, I think he has this aura that not many managers have, because he doesn’t need to speak and everyone will listen and respect him,” Konate told reporters. item.title: Cultism: Police arrest two suspects, recover locally made pistol in Ajah
item.description: By Esther Onyegbula Operatives of the Lagos State Police Command’s Violent Crime Response Unit (VCRU) have arrested two suspected cultists allegedly terrorising residents of Addo Road, Ajah, Lagos, and recovered a locally made cut-to-size pistol. The suspects, identified as Idris Rasak, 26, aka Aloss, and Ibrahim Kazeem, 25, aka Asunmo Kebe, were arrested following intelligence reports about their alleged involvement in cult-related activities in the area. The police said the suspects, during interrogation, reportedly confessed to being members of the Eiye Confraternity and subsequently led operatives to the Waterside area of Addo, Ajah, where the firearm was recovered. The development is part of efforts by the Lagos State Police Command to curb cultism and other violent crimes through intelligence-led operations. In a statement issued by the Police Public Relations Officer, Lagos State Command, SP Abimbola Adebisi, the command said the arrest followed credible intelligence on the alleged activities of the suspects. According to the statement, the operatives acted on information concerning the suspects’ alleged involvement in cult-related activities within the Addo Road area of Ajah. “During interrogation, the suspects reportedly confessed to being members of the Eiye Confraternity and led operatives to the Waterside area of Addo, Ajah, where a locally made cut-to-size pistol was recovered,” the statement said. The police said the suspects were currently in custody, while investigations were ongoing to determine the full extent of their alleged activities and identify other persons who might be connected to the reported criminal acts. The recovery of the firearm is expected to form part of the ongoing investigation as detectives work to establish the circumstances surrounding its possession and whether it was connected to any criminal activity. Cult-related violence remains a security concern in parts of Lagos, with suspected clashes and other violent incidents capable of threatening residents’ safety and disrupting normal activities in affected communities. The latest arrests underscore the importance of intelligence gathering and public cooperation in identifying suspected criminal activities and preventing violence. The Commissioner of Police, Lagos State Command, CP Tijani Fatai, reiterated the command’s commitment to tackling cultism and other criminal activities across the state. He urged members of the public to provide credible information to the police to support crime prevention and enhance the safety and security of residents. The command said it would continue to deploy intelligence-led strategies to identify and apprehend persons suspected of involvement in criminal activities. item.title: US urges citizens to ‘reconsider’ travel to Kenya after Ebola cases
item.description: The United States on Tuesday warned its citizens against travel to Kenya, raising its travel advisory after the country reported an eighth Ebola case. In the east African country’s first-ever case of the virus, a Kenyan citizen living in the Democratic Republic of Congo — where a major outbreak since May has killed more than 4,000 people — tested positive after returning home in early October. There have since been seven further cases, most in people with a close connection to the first victim, who died in the capital Nairobi on October 5. “The level was changed from Level 2 to Level 3 due to health risks,” the US embassy in Kenya said in a statement, a day after the Department of State issued renewed travel advice for its citizens. “Reconsider travel in Kenya due to risk of health, crime, kidnapping, terrorism, unrest and traffic safety. Some areas have increased risk,” it said. Kenya reported the first Ebola case on October 6 in a businessman in his forties, who lived in the DRC. He travelled by car and plane via Uganda to Kenya, where he died. The other seven cases in Kenya have been relatives of the first patient, health workers who treated him and a member of the medical support staff. Kenya’s health ministry has said they are in quarantine and in stable condition. Last week, health authorities reported that they had identified 130 contacts, 128 of whom have been traced and are in quarantine. In the DRC, the epidemic has surpassed 9,000 cases, with 4,381 deaths, according to Congolese health authorities. item.title: #EndSARS Anniversary: Police Fire Tear Gas To Disperse Gathering At Lekki Toll Gate
item.description: Tension flared at the Lekki Toll Gate as police fired tear gas to disperse activists and concerned Nigerians who gathered to commemorate the sixth anniversary of the #EndSARS protests. The gathering was organised to honour those who lost their lives and remember the demonstrations against police brutality. The protesters were forced to flee as tear gas filled the area, disrupting the planned commemoration. Among those who gathered at the toll gate were the Lagos State governorship candidates of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Funso Doherty, and the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour. ﻿ Despite the disruption, the activists vowed to continue the struggle for justice and police reforms that inspired the #EndSARS protests, while keeping alive the memory of those who died. Tension has since subsided, and the area is now clear. Police operatives use teargas to disperse a gathering at the Lekki Toll Gate during the sixth anniversary of the #EndSARS protests. Six years after the protests, the incident has renewed concerns about citizens’ right to peaceful assembly and freedom of expression. Tuesday’s incident comes six years after the protests that began in October 2020, as young Nigerians demanded an end to police brutality, particularly abuses associated with the now-disbanded Special Anti-Robbery Squad (SARS). Woman defies police teargas, honours #EndSARS victims on the sixth memorial at Lekki Tollgate The demonstrations spread across the country, with the Lekki Toll Gate becoming a focal point of the movement. On October 20, 2020, soldiers opened fire on protesters at the toll gate, an incident that remains a source of controversy over casualties and accountability. The Lagos State Judicial Panel of Inquiry, which investigated the incident, found that protesters were shot at, injured and killed. The state government later rejected key parts of the panel’s findings, including aspects of its conclusions on casualties. The anniversary has also been marked by clashes between security operatives and people who gathered at the toll gate in subsequent years. In October 2021, police fired tear gas during a memorial procession organised by youths and celebrities to honour victims of police brutality. The then Lagos Commissioner of Police, Hakeem Odumosu, said the officers were dispersing people he described as “miscreants”, rather than participants in the procession. In 2024, police again fired tear gas to disperse protesters marking the fourth anniversary. The protesters had called for the full implementation of recommendations made by judicial panels established after the 2020 demonstrations. The police said they acted after the protesters refused to disperse. The #EndSARS movement led to the disbandment of SARS in October 2020, but demands for accountability, compensation for victims and broader police reforms have continued. item.title: Gunmen kill NSCDC officer, abduct businessman in Plateau
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa Gunmen have reportedly killed a serving officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSCDC, and abducted a businessman in Pushit community, Mangu Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incident occurred at about 9:30 p.m. on Monday, despite a dusk-to-dawn curfew recently imposed in parts of the area following repeated attacks. A member of the community, Lawrence Tabitha, told newsmen that “the deceased, a Deputy Superintendent of the NSCDC, was shot near his residence while riding his motorcycle.” Tabitha said, “The gunmen had earlier abducted a businessman who deals in fuel, cement and fertiliser.” He said, “The attackers opened fire on the NSCDC officer after the headlight of his motorcycle exposed their movement as they were fleeing the area with the abducted businessman.” Tabitha said, “The incident has heightened concerns over the security situation in Pushit and surrounding communities despite measures put in place to curb attacks.” He urged security agencies and the Plateau State Government “to urgently strengthen security in Pushit District and ensure the safe release of the abducted businessman.” He said, “Residents are particularly worried by the repeated attacks recorded in communities within the district, including Vodni, Sabon Gari and Nchiya.” Tabitha appealed to residents “to remain vigilant and report suspicious movements to security agencies.” Efforts to reach security operatives for confirmation of the incident as of the time of filing this report were unsuccessful. A member of the community, Lawrence Tabitha, told newsmen that “the deceased, a Deputy Superintendent of the NSCDC, was shot near his residence while riding his motorcycle.” Tabitha said, “The gunmen had earlier abducted a businessman who deals in fuel, cement and fertiliser.” He said, “The attackers opened fire on the NSCDC officer after the headlight of his motorcycle exposed their movement as they were fleeing the area with the abducted businessman.” Tabitha said, “The incident has heightened concerns over the security situation in Pushit and surrounding communities despite measures put in place to curb attacks.” He urged security agencies and the Plateau State Government “to urgently strengthen security in Pushit District and ensure the safe release of the abducted businessman.” He said, “Residents are particularly worried by the repeated attacks recorded in communities within the district, including Vodni, Sabon Gari and Nchiya.” Tabitha appealed to residents “to remain vigilant and report suspicious movements to security agencies.” Efforts to reach security operatives for confirmation of the incident as of the time of filing this report were unsuccessful. item.title: Abduction of corps members: DSS arraigns five suspects
item.description: By Emmanuel Iheaka The Department of State Services has arraigned three suspects, namely Usman Aliyu, Babangida Aliyu and Mohammed Ali, over the kidnapping of 20 NYSC corps members along the Owerri-Onitsha road. The three suspects pleaded not guilty to the three-count charge of abduction and hostage taking, collection of ransom of N48 million and dollars, as well as illegal possession of firearms. The other two suspects, Aminu Haliru and Jiji Ibrahim, were charged with conspiracy and hostage-taking, and illegal possession of firearms. They were accused of abducting Winner Ogidi, Opara Timothy, Ogechi Henrietta and one other on October 4, 2026, but they also pleaded not guilty to the charges. Counsel for the state, Ekezie Nwauzo, filed a motion for the suspects to remain in the DSS custody, which the court presided over by Hon. Justice Emeka Orafu granted. Nnaemeka Adipuo stood for the first and second defendants in the case of abduction of corps members, while Paschal Ofoma represented the third defendant. The cases were adjourned to Thursday, October 22; Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, October 27, 28, 29, for hearing. Recall that about 20 corps members had been reportedly abducted on October 1, along Owerri-Onitsha Road, while heading to the NYSC orientation camps in Akwa Ibom and Abia States. They were later released after about six days in captivity and subsequently reunited with their families. Speaking to journalists after the court session, counsels for the defendants, Adipuo and Ofoma, noted that the suspects are presumed innocent until proven guilty. item.title: ‘He let Manchester United down’ – Ten Hag recounts fallout with Ronaldo
item.description: Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has accused Cristiano Ronaldo of letting both the club and him down during their time together at Old Trafford, alleging that the Portuguese forward failed to meet the team’s fitness and training standards. Ten Hag made the remarks in an exclusive interview with The Athletic on Tuesday, reflecting on his difficult relationship with the five-time Ballon d’Or winner during his tenure as United manager. “He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him,” Ten Hag said. “I flew out to Portugal to speak with him about what I was aiming for before I came to United.” Despite his criticism, the Dutchman acknowledged Ronaldo’s place in football history, describing him as one of the game’s greatest players. “Obviously, he’s one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision,” he added. Ten Hag also alleged that Ronaldo struggled to meet the club’s fitness requirements, claiming that the forward sometimes withdrew from training sessions and failed to achieve the required heart rate levels. He also recalled an incident after United’s 4-0 defeat to Brentford in August 2022, when players had to run laps as punishment. According to Ten Hag, Ronaldo completed only two of the three laps. The former manager said he confronted Ronaldo over his fitness and positioning, insisting that the forward needed to work harder to put himself in scoring positions. “I confronted him with this,” Ten Hag said. “Many times I say, ‘Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can’t bring yourself in the box, you can’t score’. He was not capable to do this.” Ten Hag also claimed that Ronaldo did not contribute sufficiently to the team’s pressing and defensive work, alleging that the forward encouraged teammates to conserve their energy during training. “Ronaldo was telling the players: save your legs at training,” he said. “I understand it when you are top fit, but first you have to train yourself to get into the right fitness levels.” The Dutchman maintained that while managers must accommodate their best players, star footballers must also accept their responsibilities to the team. “Every top team has to embrace the top player, but the top player has to work for the team,” Ten Hag said. Ronaldo’s relationship with Ten Hag deteriorated during the 2022/23 season, culminating in the forward’s departure from Manchester United in November 2022 following a controversial interview in which he criticised the club and its management. Ten Hag made the remarks in an exclusive interview with The Athletic on Tuesday, reflecting on his difficult relationship with the five-time Ballon d’Or winner during his tenure as United manager. “He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him,” Ten Hag said. “I flew out to Portugal to speak with him about what I was aiming for before I came to United.” Despite his criticism, the Dutchman acknowledged Ronaldo’s place in football history, describing him as one of the game’s greatest players. “Obviously, he’s one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision,” he added. Ten Hag also alleged that Ronaldo struggled to meet the club’s fitness requirements, claiming that the forward sometimes withdrew from training sessions and failed to achieve the required heart rate levels. He also recalled an incident after United’s 4-0 defeat to Brentford in August 2022, when players had to run laps as punishment. According to Ten Hag, Ronaldo completed only two of the three laps. The former manager said he confronted Ronaldo over his fitness and positioning, insisting that the forward needed to work harder to put himself in scoring positions. “I confronted him with this,” Ten Hag said. “Many times I say, ‘Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can’t bring yourself in the box, you can’t score’. He was not capable to do this.” Ten Hag also claimed that Ronaldo did not contribute sufficiently to the team’s pressing and defensive work, alleging that the forward encouraged teammates to conserve their energy during training. “Ronaldo was telling the players: save your legs at training,” he said. “I understand it when you are top fit, but first you have to train yourself to get into the right fitness levels.” The Dutchman maintained that while managers must accommodate their best players, star footballers must also accept their responsibilities to the team. “Every top team has to embrace the top player, but the top player has to work for the team,” Ten Hag said. Ronaldo’s relationship with Ten Hag deteriorated during the 2022/23 season, culminating in the forward’s departure from Manchester United in November 2022 following a controversial interview in which he criticised the club and its management. item.title: China opposes US ban on govt agencies from using DeepSeek
item.description: Beijing opposed on Tuesday a US government ban on its agencies using AI tools from Chinese startup DeepSeek, saying the move “overstretched” the concept of national security. China and the United States are locked in a race for dominance in the fast-moving artificial intelligence sector, trading accusations of stealing AI technologies and jeopardising security in recent months. The US Department of Homeland Security on Monday banned products developed by DeepSeek — and tools created using DeepSeek by third parties — saying they risked sharing sensitive data with China. Beijing’s foreign ministry opposed the ban on Tuesday, vowing to protect Chinese businesses. “China has consistently opposed the overstretching of the concept of national security and the politicisation of issues related to science, technology, and trade,” ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told a news conference. The Department of Homeland Security can issue directions to civilian agencies, but not the military or intelligence services. Its statement on Monday said that “DeepSeek’s models multiple threat vectors” and must be removed from IT devices. Use of DeepSeek AI tools “may result in the transfer of sensitive data to (China) if used by US government employees or vendors,” the department warned. Its servers are located in China, where the legal system permits the government “extensive authority” to access private company infrastructure, it said. AFP has contacted DeepSeek for comment. DeepSeek, one of China’s top AI labs, shook up the industry in January 2025 with a low-cost, high-performance chatbot, challenging assumptions of US dominance. The firm released a long-awaited new model, V4, in April and this month updated a faster, more lightweight version of V4. The United States has accused DeepSeek and other top Chinese AI firms of systematically stealing the capabilities of cutting-edge models developed by American rivals. Despite their fierce competition in the field, China and the United States in September agreed to set up a “communication channel” for AI incidents. The topic is expected to arise again when the countries’ leaders meet next month at a summit in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. item.content:encoded: F resh controversies have resurfaced over the redeployment of key personnel of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) ahead of the 2027 general elections. In the recent changes at INEC, Mrs Oluyemi Titilayo Adeyemi-Showunmi, formerly the Administrative Secretary of the commission’s Lagos State office, was redeployed as the Director of Electoral Operations at the commission. She is the wife of Segun Showunmi, a spokesman for the Tinubu/Shettima 2027 Presidential Campaign Council. Prof. Mustapha Aliu, identified as an elder brother of Sokoto State Governor, Ahmed Aliyu, who is seeking a second term on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), has also been nominated as an INEC commissioner. According to reports, Isah Magaji Gummi, who previously headed the Electoral Operations Department, was redeployed to the Voter Registry Department. Fubara, Wike reconciliation: Rivers Assembly recalls 3 lawmakers 27 kidnap victims rescued in Katsina The Electoral Operations Department plays a key role in election planning and implementation, including the coordination of polling arrangements, deployment of election materials and management of personnel involved in electoral operations. Although the director of the department does not independently determine election results, the responsibilities attached to the office have drawn attention to the redeployment and calls for INEC to explain the considerations behind the decision. Adeyemi-Showunmi’s redeployment has sparked debate among civil society organisations and on social media over transparency, political neutrality and public confidence in the electoral body. Former director of voter education at INEC, Mr Nick Dazang, when contacted said, it would be wrong for the Commission to pretend that appointing someone that close to a sitting governor who is contesting elections has no implications. “The person may be eminently qualified but I have profound misgivings if he can discharge or execute his office as Resident Electoral Commissioner with the professionalism, neutrality and impartiality that the office demands. On the redeployment of Sowunmi wife, he said in the time past, and oblivious of the closeness/proximity of INEC officials to certain politically exposed persons, INEC officials on their merit, had been inadvertently assigned to roles/tasks that put them in difficult positions which complicated the Commission’s core values of impartiality and neutrality. He said In such circumstances, and in deference to its core values, INEC has demonstrated sensitivity by not posting such deserving officials to these positions. “It is likely that the Commission may not be aware or cognizant of the said officer’s relationship with a prominent politician. “But once this is established, and its attention is called to this reality, it should promptly do the needful, namely: not to put the officer in a position that compromises the Commission’s principles of neutrality and provision of a level playing field to all contestants. In the prevailing circumstance, the officer should be directed to recuse herself. This will allay fears, rightly or wrongly, that she has been procured to deliberately confer an advantage to any candidate(s) in the election. Either the tenure of the subsisting Director is specially extended for the period of the election, or his Deputy is directed to act in the position of Director, subject to consideration(s) of merit, federal character and the core values aforementioned,” he added. Director-General of YIAGA Africa, Samson Itodo, warned that the electoral body must ensure public confidence in the electoral process and should not take the people for granted in its appointment. On the appointment of Adeyemi-Showunmi as INEC Director of Electoral Operations, Itodo said elections are fundamentally about operations, adding that by this token, it is one of the most sensitive and consequential departments within INEC. He said, “In fact, the Electoral Operations Department is at the heart of election administration. From the recruitment and deployment of polling officials to the planning, production and distribution of election materials, as well as the operational arrangements for voting and results collation, the department plays a central role in determining how elections are conducted. “Mrs. Showunmi’s competence and professional capacity are not in doubt. However, competence alone is not sufficient for appointments to sensitive positions in election management. The independence, impartiality and perceived neutrality of those entrusted with managing elections are equally important. “Appointing individuals with strong ties to politicians in such strategic positions inevitably raises legitimate questions about impartiality and INEC independence. These concerns become even more pronounced in a climate of deep public distrust, growing fears of political capture of INEC, and politicians boldly declaring the number of votes they expect to secure before a single ballot has been cast. “At a time when public confidence in the electoral process is already fragile, appointments to critical positions within INEC should inspire confidence, not deepen suspicion. INEC must recognize that its credibility rests not only on the technical competence of its personnel but also on public confidence in INEC’s independence from partisan interests. Public confidence in the electoral process must never be taken for granted. In this instance, it is being taken for granted,” he said. Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar was among those who first raised the alarm over the issue, demanding immediate and full transparency from INEC. In a statement issued by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said the reported changes in the Electoral Operations Department raised serious questions that INEC must answer without delay. “Reports indicate that Director Isa Magaji Gummi was moved from Electoral Operations to the Voter Registry Department, while Mrs Oluyemi Titilayo Adeyemi-Showunmi was appointed to head Electoral Operations. Dr Lawrence Bayode has also been identified as the head of Information and Communication Technology (ICT). “These departments are at the heart of election administration. INEC must explain these decisions, publish the criteria applied and show that every appointment and redeployment followed due process, was based on merit and was free from political interference. Nigerians will not accept vague assurances on matters this serious.” Atiku said no official should be presumed compromised because of their ethnicity, background or associations. But when reported political connections or a concentration of appointments raises public concern, INEC must provide verifiable assurances that its impartiality is protected. “A government that has driven millions of Nigerians into hardship must not be allowed to turn the electoral umpire into an instrument of political survival. When sensitive election departments are reshaped and major contracts are surrounded by unanswered questions, the suspicion that a failing administration is seeking every possible advantage to cling to power will only grow. INEC must dispel that suspicion through full, immediate and verifiable disclosure,” he said. A political analyst, Professor Saleh Dauda, maintained that political undertones cannot be ruled out in the redeployment of Adeyemi-Showunmi ahead of the general elections.
